text:
lee: Morning sync: ran a 30m window with ingress coalescer + adaptive batching. Seeing a recurring p95 host-parse bump (~+9%) tied to mixed-length micro-batches.
maya: any profiler output?
lee: pasted trimmed stacks: parse_stream -> frame_reassemble -> tokenize_accumulate -> utf8_normalize -> kvcache_lookup.
rohan: that chain smells like two problems: tokenize reallocs + extra remote KV lookups when streams are merged.
maya: how big are the mixed batches? distribution shows many batches with sizes [1,2,8,40] in same minibatch. seq stddev often > 3.5. kernel selector then picks conservative kernel a lot.
lee: exact. when kernel switches to fallback we see downstream model time slightly lower but host preproc jumps, net result p95 decode + tail.
perf-bot: trace 1769995600 uploaded.
rohan: quick hypothesis: coalescer merging without affinity causes per-batch KV fanout. kvcache miss rate up ~2.7% in those windows. eviction bursts align with the worst tails.
maya: run small sim: if coalescer respects seq-buckets (tiny/medium/large) mixed_batch_rate drops ~68% and p95 host-parse falls ~7%.
lee: good. micro-optimizations also helped: pre-reserve token buffers cut allocate churn (median tokenize_accumulate 0.42ms->0.13ms in harness). ascii fastpath removed utf8 normalize for ~60% of payloads, saving ~0.11ms median.
rohan: love the wins. But watch memory: pre-reserve increases per-worker RSS. We should implement pooled slabs with per-worker caps and a recycle window. on dense nodes cap should be low.
maya: on KV side, proposing a short routing affinity window (30s) to keep repeated user's shards on same kvcache shard. Sim dropped eviction spikes ~35% but watch hotspots.
lee: agree, but must implement soft TTL and random jitter to avoid long-term hotspotting. also add per-shard load shedding if one shard gets >X qps.
rohan: kernel selector change: clamp variance before decision by capping lengths to the 95th percentile when computing stddev (cheap and limits outlier influence). We'll expose as toggle flag.
maya: and coalescer change: prefer to flush current micro-batch if preproc backlog > 1.2ms to avoid tail amplification. Flagged as runtime param.
lee: ingress differences: http/1.1 still worse — header-frag parsing and chunk reassembly expensive. grpc p95 host-parse ~1.6ms vs http1 ~2.8ms in canary.
rohan: short-term ingress fix: enable header-frag coalescer to merge header fragments before parse and enable keepalive/writev when available. longer-term: encourage http2 for internal flows or proxy-coalesce at edge.
maya: observability: add metrics: mixed_batch_rate, kernel_mispredict_rate, kvcache_per_batch_lookups, slab_pool_rss, host_parse_p95_by_route.
lee: created dashboard and alert for mixed_batch_rate > 1% and kernel_mispredict_rate > 0.5%.
perf-bot: ticket PERF-8123 created: "ingress coalesce + kernel selector feedback" assigned to lee,maya,rohan.
rohan: action items: 1) coalescer: seq-bucketing + flush-on-backlog toggle (maya), 2) kernel: variance-clamp flag + metric (rohan), 3) tokenize: pre-reserve + pooled slab w/ cap (lee), 4) kvcache: short affinity window + eviction dashboards (maya), 5) ingress: header-frag coalesce toggle (infra).
maya: I'll push coalescer bucket PR as feature-flagged and include sim traces.
lee: I'll open slab+pre-reserve PR with microbench and memory graphs; default cap conservative.
rohan: I'll land selector clamp behind flag and add kernel_mispredict_rate to telemetry.
infra: will enable header-frag coalesce toggle in canary and monitor host_parse_p95.
lee: timeline: land flags today, canary at 10% tonight, collect 4 windows, iterate. aim to get host_parse_p95 under 1.2ms for short chats.
maya: if we achieve that we should see ~5-8% reduction in overall decode tail.
rohan: one more note: guard the ASCII fastpath with a quick is_ascii() scan to avoid misclassifying. add metric for ascii_fastpath_skipped_count.
lee: good point. also add a mem-guard that disables pre-reserve if worker RSS > cap.
maya: thanks team. will post PR links in thread. :thumbsup:
